scopeNote: General tracking for eligible open-permit categories. Family-member, IEC, protection and public-policy routes have distinct instructions; this tracker does not establish eligibility or replace them. Community averages combine applications within this guide and are not IRCC processing estimates.

relatedPathways.label: Canadian Experience Class
relatedPathways.description: Qualifying Canadian work may support CEC eligibility. Work gained while studying full-time does not count toward the CEC minimum. Meeting eligibility does not guarantee an invitation.

relatedPathways.label: Provincial nominee programs
relatedPathways.description: Check the province’s current stream rules, selection process and settlement-intent requirements. A permit alone does not qualify you for nomination or guarantee PR.

steps.title: Identify your eligible open-permit category
steps.description: Use IRCC’s finder to confirm a category such as an eligible family-member permit. This is a general tracker; follow the category’s special instructions. PGWP and bridging permits have their own MaplePath roadmaps.

preparationChecklist.text: Open the specific category’s official requirements before proceeding.

officialLinks.label: Find the work permit you need

commonMistakes: An open work permit is not available simply because you want to work.

steps.title: Prepare category-specific evidence
steps.description: Confirm the current rules for your category. Family members may need relationship evidence and proof that the principal applicant meets the applicable study or work criteria; IEC has its own invitation process.

requiredDocuments.title: Evidence required for your qualifying category
requiredDocuments.condition: Include when required by your IRCC checklist or the linked instructions.

preparationChecklist.text: Use your category’s instructions for eligibility, forms and fees.

steps.title: Choose the correct application instructions
steps.description: Use the inside-Canada or outside-Canada process that applies to your eligibility. Merely being in Canada does not qualify you for an in-Canada application.

steps.description: Keep your status valid and review any future application before expiry. Canadian study or work can be relevant to some PR programs, but a permit does not grant permanent residence.
